lesson_title: Staircases, Snowballs and the Cube Law: Patterns, Finance and Measurement Essentials
hook_text: Double every side of a box. The volume doesn't double. It doesn't even quadruple.
clip_script: Feel its violence with k equals three. A solid of volume fifty becomes fifty times twenty-seven — one thousand three hundred and fifty. Not three times bigger: twenty-seven times bigger. And the reverse trap: doubling every side of a box does not double the volume; it multiplies it by eight. Double ONLY the radius of a cylinder: volume is pi r squared h, and the radius appears squared, so the volume multiplies by four — not eight, because the height never moved. The law reads letter by letter: each scaled length contributes its own factor, as many times as it appears in the formula.
visual_style: A small box swells to eight ghost-copies of itself stacked two by two by two; then a cylinder's radius stretches while its height stays pinned, and four glowing copies fill the widened tin; the powers k, k squared, k cubed stamp themselves onto a length, a face and a solid in turn.
mood: Playful shock — the innocent 'double it' revealed as an eight-fold explosion.
pacing: Slow build on the doubled box, sharp reveal of the eight copies, brisk letter-by-letter payoff on the cylinder.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and give every power its dimension before November does.
